 Home / Tripura News / Story #43240 Tripura News 3 MIN READ 597 READS Cyclone Akvan's outer influence to bring three days of rain in Tripura; IMD issues heavy rain alert for four districts
 TRIPURATIMES Desk
 Agartala • 19 Nov 2026, 02:50 PM
 Text Size: A- A A+ Tripura is expected to experience cloudy skies, intermittent rainfall and isolated thunderstorms over the next three days under the indirect influence of Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal. However, weather experts have clarified that there is no threat of a direct cyclonic strike or severe wind impact on the state, even as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued heavy rainfall alerts for several districts. 
 Providing an update on the evolving weather situation, IMD scientist Partha Roy said the rainfall being recorded across parts of Tripura is linked to the outer circulation of the cyclonic system currently moving towards the Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh coast. While the cyclone itself remains far from the state, its expansive outer cloud bands are transporting moisture into the region, resulting in overcast conditions and scattered rainfall. 
 According to meteorological officials, the outer band of the cyclone extends several hundred kilometres from the core system, allowing its influence to reach northeastern states despite the cyclone tracking along the eastern coastline of India. This moisture influx is expected to keep weather conditions unsettled across Tripura for the next few days. 
 The IMD has issued weather advisories for Thursday and Friday, warning of thunderstorms accompanied by gusty winds reaching speeds of 30 to 40 kilometres per hour at isolated locations in every district. While thunderstorm activity may persist in some areas on November 22, meteorologists do not anticipate any significant damage from wind-related activity during that period. 
 Particular attention has been drawn to the possibility of heavy rainfall in parts of the state. A yellow alert has been issued for South Tripura, Gomati and Sepahijala districts for Thursday. For Friday and Saturday, the alert area widens, with isolated heavy rainfall expected in West Tripura, Sepahijala, Gomati and South Tripura districts. 
 Despite the warnings, weather officials have stressed that the current conditions should not be interpreted as a sign of a major cyclone threat. Partha Roy clarified that all anticipated weather developments are linked solely to the indirect influence of Cyclone Akvan and that there are currently no indications of severe cyclonic conditions affecting Tripura directly. 
 The weather pattern is also expected to influence seasonal temperatures. According to the IMD, temperatures across the state are likely to remain close to normal for this time of year. Officials explained that cyclonic systems over the Bay of Bengal often slow the onset of cooler weather by increasing cloud cover and atmospheric moisture, preventing a rapid drop in temperature. 
 Meteorologists are also looking ahead to the winter season. Roy indicated that the IMD is likely to begin issuing fog-related forecasts from next week once the cyclone's influence weakens and weather conditions stabilise. Regular winter forecasting operations are expected to commence from the beginning of December. 
 Authorities have advised residents, particularly those living in districts under heavy rainfall alerts, to stay informed through official IMD bulletins and weather updates. While no major threat is currently anticipated, officials emphasised the importance of remaining aware of rapidly changing weather conditions during the cyclone's indirect influence on the region.
